questions.q: What is the Law of Accelerating Returns?
a: Evolution and technology keep speeding up
Resources become scarcer as populations grow
Creativity declines steadily as people age
Education improves at a constant rate
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the shrinking gaps between inventions to show that change keeps accelerating.

Inherited talent
Random inspiration
Technical expertise
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines creativity as imagination applied in the real world.

questions.q: What three mediums does creativity get channeled into?
a: Physical, sensory and cognitive
Visual, verbal and digital
Social, financial and artistic
Natural, mechanical and abstract
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists physical, sensory and cognitive as the three kinds of creative mediums.

questions.q: What common fear keeps people from being creative at work?
a: Believing they alone will be blamed if ideas fail
Believing their colleagues are more talented
Believing creativity is only for artists
Believing new ideas take too much time
questions.why: Lesson 3 says one pitfall is fearing that we alone will be blamed when ideas fail.

questions.q: What does Robinson say about rules and creativity?
a: Rules can provide a frame you step out of at times
Rules must be removed entirely for ideas to flow
Rules only apply to artistic kinds of work
Rules guarantee predictable, safe results
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues rules create a frame of control that you can step out of at times.
